notes: kb/Work PB5174 landed. §1985:VI.5.9.3 SR3: "The lowercase letters corresponding to the uppercase letters representing the PICTURE symbols A, B, P, S, V, X, Z, CR, and DB are equivalent to their uppercase representations in a PICTURE character-string. All other lowercase letters are not equivalent to their corresponding uppercase representations." PictureAnalyzer.FoldPictureCase is the one fold the character-string is read through: below 2002 it folds only a b p s v x z c r d, so pic aaa, s9v9, zz9, xbx and 99cr bind as their uppercase forms, and under CURRENCY SIGN IS "W" the letter w stays lowercase, is no currency symbol (AnalyzeCharacterString's scan compares the folded symbol, no second fold) and draws COBOL0808 (SR2's whitelist). Witnesses: 1985-SR-VI_5_9_3-3 (the equivalent letters) and pb5174-lowercase-currency-letter-85 (PIC w99 refused at 85).

next.reason: 1985 makes only the lowercase forms of A, B, P, S, V, X, Z, CR and DB equivalent, and 'All other lowercase letters are not equivalent', which includes a letter chosen as the currency symbol. §2023:13.18.40.3 SR3 refers symbols other than the currency symbol to §2023:8.1.3.2 GR3, under which basic letters outside literals are 'treated in a case-insensitive manner'. It refers currency symbols to §2023:12.3.7.3 SR20, whose NOTE 2 says 'N'M', N'm', 'M', and 'm' used as currency symbols are all equivalent'. A lowercase occurrence of a letter currency symbol, not equivalent in 1985, is equivalent in 2023.
